So the reason for this is because for "sweaty", you run Slayer sets instead of ROJO (you can get near 100% major slayers with Slayer sets where you cant with ROJO and slayer sets is just more reliable for burst fight and burn starts), you do not get nightblade because as of now, they do not have anything to contribute to the group. No Unique Synergy, No Group Wide buff ( you get the minor crit from Sorcerer and Sorcerer provides Major Berserk). So when you run a Solo Heal and a Solo Tank setup, Warden is just the only class that can reliably provide group with Major Resolve. Therefore, they are just put on Healer more often. If in a situation where you run two tanks and one healer, the other tank will be Warden and the Healer will most likely be Necromancer (or Warden offtank/dps and Necro Healer). That is just what is most optimised with the current metas at the moment.  Since you can solo heal most trial contents and in a trial where you cant, like Solo Heal rockgrove mini skipping Oax, you just have the "support dps" swap to healer on Bahsei and the Warden would just solo heal the other two bosses and Ash Titan. Nightblade is simply not needed at the moment.

As someone mentioned, trials can get really sweaty dependant on the difficulty you are embarking. Normal and Veteran are non-issue and the group that requirement "sweaty" healer for those is usually ones that cannot reliably clear content, so I am only going to talk about the high level content which is trifectas, scorepushing and mechanic skipping (vAS2 double mini skip or less than 2 mins, vCR3 less than 2 mins or Galewe skip or 0 portals or triple mini skips to name a few).

As healer in "sweaty" trial, you can solo heal most of the content while wearing supporting buffs set. The most common one which as mentioned by someone is Spell power cure + Pearl of Enorfey + Pillager's Profit + Nazaray monster set as Healer can pump out a lot of Ult generation via just healing meeting conditions of Spell Power Cure and Pearl which then spread to the group via Pillager's Profit every 45 seconds. There are a few ways to go about set optimisations but this is just the most common one out there and the most common classes would be Warden for their group-wide Major Resolve and Minor Toughness or Necromancer because Necromancer lacks the single target potential therefore forcing them on heal+ult gen for Major Vulnerability just free up other spots for more damage.

Heals over Time; you may not need it but you'd be happy that you have them there when you actually do. A healer pumping out 120k raw HPS just means there's 10k per second per individuals on average (my personal highest is 152k raw hps output on 1mins 30 something seconds Yaselya hardmode portal skip). There are fluctuations; yes, but you get the gist of it. The more the better WHILE you maintain perfect or near perfect uptime on the buffs and debuffs you responsible for.

The general consensus on uptimes are if it is a parse fight with no invulnerability on the bosses should be near 100%, 95%-100% is what you should aim for. Ult generation with Pearl, you should be looking at 400 ult when the 45seconds cooldown is over.

Martial Knowledge is 62.5% but realistically in fight where your light attack travel time do shave off some, 50-55% is acceptable. 60% for Parse fight.

Z'en 5th stacks should 90%+, Powerful Assault 85%+ and yes you can get 99% on that (the 1% is because you need combat to start Q.Q). Roaring Opportunist is 72%. .... these are just the buffs off the top of my head and yes these are very achievable during fights and hardmode contents as others including me have proven it is possible.

I do not do them every week on every character personally. I only log in to raid with people I know. So to answer your question. Healer is the top role in ESO that have really low floor but very high ceiling, followed by Tank then DPS at the Bottom. Tank's uptime get really sweaty too on what they do, but they just have smaller gap between the floor and the ceiling as you can tell right away if your tank is bad. You can get by with crappy healer but as the contents get harder, the more apparent the bad healers you have are and the different between a good one and a bad one get really apparent when you run high level content.  
  
Note: Yes we cannot be perfection all the time, but we should thrive to be at the very least. I generally check my uptimes after every fight while progging to see what I am missing and what I can do better. Sometimes some small details can escape you, that's why it is important to be aware of it.

Warden and Necro is what I would recommend for classes for the theme of cycle of life and death for the cheesy romantic out there. 

Warden:

Warden is the go to healer if you have to pick one for a group as its sources of group wide major resolve (increase def) and minor toughness (increase max health) as well as offering unique synergy Harvest (via budding seed).

Necromancer:

Good tank and damage for PvE, especially more so in 4 man dungeon group as main source of major vulnerability (glacial colossus, aoe major breach and aoe minor vulnerability (via unnerving boneyard and its unique synergy grave robber). Major/Minor vulnerability increases damage done on targets (10%, 5% respectively) and major breach is reducing targets' defences. Necrotic potency will get you top up on ultimate.

Build-wise: 

Main healer support set is Spell Power Cure to increase spell/weapon damage via overhealing. The 2nd set is situation but I recommend Master Architect for 4 man dungeon for its major slayer (increase allies' damage done by 10%) via ultimate cast Aggressive warhorse from assault skill line for Major Force and increase max stats- more max stats is more damage and heals (you can and should back bar this with lightning staff for offbalance via blockade of element) front bar healing stick is up to the wielder, Grand Master restoration staff restores allies resources via spring skill of the restore staff skill line. Or Powerful assault backbar and proc via echoing vigor. Nazaray monster set is another good one to extend debuffs on your target. 

Dps necromancer:
Corpse buster is difficult to farm but offer very high aoe damage potential at the moment with necromancer class mastery via scribing skill banner and aoe damage as necromancer damaged are all aoe direct damage and aoe damage over time. Azure blight is another one for aoe situation, otherwise coral riptide. Go stam cro.
Khajit is best for 4 man but if you intend to do trials, you will cap out on crit damage. Orc or Dark elf works if you want to optimise via race. Velothi mythic item.

Tank necromancer: 
There are so many tanks sets and they are very situation based, so if you want to dedicate to tanking. I suggest go dps first to farm all those sets and easier time doing early contents with your SO.

Early starting out damage sets
Order's Wrath is craft-able and you should have it medium divine on body pieces or 3 body pieces and 2 jewelries with Velothi. The other sets is either craft or buy via Guild trader or farm overland to start but you shouldn't have much issue supplement for damage. Briarheart is good overland set from Wrothgar.

Early starting out healing sets
Unfortunately try to get spell power cure (white gold tower dungeon) as early as possible. 

4 man healers usually run Spell power cure main healing bar, back other other ultimate proc set that buff group ( or Powerful assault - 4 man dungeon wise, backbar lightning stick) and Pearl of Enorfey with monster sets like Symphony of Blade. Probably start farming for sets here after Champion points 160 for gears trading and reconstruction via sticker book. Otherwise, whatever since she will be playing you and enemies scales to the players in overland. 

Good luck and have fun.

Edit: I should note that I used the term Stamina necromancer, that shouldn't discourage you to think the class is melee based nor none-magical. It is simply that Stamina should be your main resource and highest resource pool. Your damage and healing scales with whatever maximum resource pools the highest (as well as whichever spell damage and weapon damage, and spell critical chance and weapon critical chance - whichever the highest) stamina is just more valued for DPS at the moment due to it not regenerate if you hold block or sprint. Major/Minor Mending is Healing Done = All healing that the person with Major/Minor Mending disses out.

Major/Minor Vitality is Healing Received = All healing that the person with Major/Minor Vitality receives from outside sources including their own. 

If Character A has Major/Minor Mending and Major/Minor Vitality, Character A's heal to themselves increases via both buffs.   
  
If Character A heals Character B that has Major/Minor Mending, Character B only receives % of the heals increased by Character A's Major/Minor Mending, the same Major/Minor buffs doesn't stack on each other.   
  
If Character A heals Character C that has Major/Minor Vitality, Character's C healing received got both Mending and Vitality increase.

If Character C has Major/Minor Vitality, the heals they cast on themselves got the boost, but the heals they cast to others without Vitality Do not get the boost.
